structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE architecture/design document for the Pre-Python gate at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/work-and-release.md, covering BIU/work authority, lifecycle, external mappings, readiness versus release, rework/closure outcomes, and multi-repository DAG completion, using cited local source material without implementing code or treating the candidate as Founder-approved architecture.
structuredContent.summary: The proposed work is a bounded documentation-only design packet with explicit scope, authorized paths, source baselines, exclusions, acceptance criteria, and governing architectural authority. It is cohesive despite spanning BIU, lifecycle, and release policy because those concepts form one work-and-release contract. No material owner decision appears necessary before drafting; unresolved Founder-level decisions are to be explicitly recorded in the candidate rather than silently resolved.
implementation_unknowns: Where the cited local source materials are located and which exact sections provide the strongest traceability for each required invariant and example.

How to reconcile any tension among BIU history, lifecycle correction/reset material, Node operational behavior, and EOS candidate conformance pins without treating candidate material as adopted authority.

The exact set of successful and failing example scenarios that best demonstrate ambiguous mapping rejection, cross-role result rejection, release ON/OFF guards, duplicate-release denial, accepted-result-changing rework invalidation, and multi-repository DAG completion.
The local packet/readiness evidence format to use for the candidate work-unit receipts, if not already obvious from existing templates.
Whether a documentation checker already exists for path/coverage validation and how to invoke or cite it in evidence without performing runtime regression work.
independent_decision_centers: Candidate BIU/work-and-release design artifact for Pre-Python architecture documentation, bounded to one document and local evidence.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable by reviewing the produced document and local evidence against the stated G07/G08/G09 rows, binding architecture authority, binding implementation gate, global exclusions, and source/invariant mapping requirements. One independent content review can provide a meaningful verdict because the output is a single candidate design artifact with explicit traceability, examples, scope limitations, unresolved Founder decisions, and no operational side effects. Runtime regression verification is not required for this documentation-only task, though source citations and coverage/path checks remain relevant.
material_risks: The document could accidentally present candidate architecture/security/storage semantics as approved authority rather than labeling them CANDIDATE and recording Founder-review needs.
The author could invent new decisions instead of reusing and mapping the cited source material.
The document could implicitly adopt neighboring or EOS draft material beyond the stated conformance pin and accepted EOS requirements.
The work could drift into implementation, source/test/config changes, service/profile/secrets/GitHub changes, or Python implementation planning beyond the authorized documentation scope.
Lifecycle and release semantics could be conflated, especially READY versus automatic release ON/OFF, dispatch versus lifecycle, or merge versus closure.
External workflow mappings could be made ambiguous or adapter-specific in a way that violates the Anti-Corruption Layer and repository-neutral work model.
Multi-repository completion could be incorrectly modeled as atomic repository mutation rather than explicit DAG completion across bounded artifacts.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed with the documentation handoff: draft the single candidate design document and local packet/readiness evidence, keeping all proposed architecture semantics explicitly candidate, tracing each invariant to cited source authority, and recording any genuine Founder decisions encountered rather than resolving them silently.
structuredContent.rationale: The controlling condition is readiness, not approval. The task supplies clear governing intent, authorized locations, baseline/source evidence, explicit exclusions, acceptance criteria, and authority boundaries. Remaining uncertainty is normal engineering/documentation research about locating and reconciling cited evidence, not unresolved owner intent. Although the work touches several architecture topics, they are semantically coupled as one BIU/work-and-release contract and can be independently reviewed or rejected as a single document. Rework is expected to be localized to the candidate artifact and its evidence unless the author discovers an actual contradiction requiring Founder escalation.
